member.name: T:Meziantou.Framework.Globbing.Glob
member.summary:
Glob patterns specify sets of filenames with wildcard characters. Supported syntaxes:
Wildcard Description
* matches any number of characters including none, excluding directory separator
? matches a single character
[abc] matches one character in the brackets
[!abc] matches any character not in the brackets. , and also accept [^abc].
[a-z] matches one character from the range given in the brackets. With GlobOptions.IgnoreCase, a character matches when it, its lowercase form or its uppercase form is in the range.
[!a-z] matches one character that is not from the range given in the brackets, using the same rule as [a-z] for GlobOptions.IgnoreCase.
[[:alpha:]] matches one character of a POSIX character class. Only supported by , and . The supported classes are alnum, alpha, blank, cntrl, digit, graph, lower, print, punct, space, upper and xdigit. With GlobOptions.IgnoreCase, upper and lower match a letter of either case.
[[=a=]] [[.a.]] an equivalence class and a collating symbol, which both stand for the character they hold. Only supported by and . A collating symbol can be a range bound: [[.-.]-0].
{abc,123} comma-delimited set of literals, matches 'abc' or '123'. Only supported by ; the other dialects read the braces as ordinary characters.
** matches zero or more directories when it makes a whole path segment. A trailing ** matches at least one segment. The POSIX dialects read it as a *.
!pattern leading '!' negates the pattern. Only supported by and .
\x escapes the following character. For instance, '\*' matches the literal character '*' instead of being a wildcard. and the POSIX dialects also read an escape in a bracket expression. reads '\' as a path separator and escapes a character with %XX instead.
If the pattern ends with a /, only directories are matched. Otherwise, only files are matched. A pattern matches both a file and a directory, and one ending with a / matches the directory itself as well as everything below it. A pattern matches a plain string, whatever the kind of item.
, , and follow the behavior of git, MSBuild and fnmatch(3), which the tests check against corpora produced by those implementations. The exceptions are deliberate: characters are compared as UTF-16 code units (git compares the bytes of their UTF-8 encoding), a path ending with a / is a directory (fnmatch compares strings), and a pattern that can never match anything, such as one holding an unknown character class, is rejected.
Matching backtracks, so the cost of a single call grows exponentially with the number of * wildcards in one path segment. Ordinary patterns and file names are unaffected, but a pattern coming from an untrusted source can be made expensive on purpose. Bound the length and the wildcard count of such patterns before parsing them.

member.summary: Specifies the glob pattern dialect to use when parsing a pattern.

member.name: F:Meziantou.Framework.Globbing.GlobDialect.Standard
member.summary: Use the default glob pattern syntax: *, ?, **, bracket expressions, {a,b} sets, \ escapes and a leading ! to negate the pattern. Wildcards do not match a leading dot unless is set.

member.name: F:Meziantou.Framework.Globbing.GlobDialect.Git
member.summary: Use gitignore pattern syntax, as described by gitignore(5) and implemented by git's wildmatch: a pattern without a / matches a name at any depth, a leading / anchors it, and a trailing / only matches directories. Bracket expressions accept ^ as a negation, escapes and character classes such as [[:alpha:]], and braces are ordinary characters. An entry that git can never match, such as one holding an unterminated bracket expression, is rejected.

member.name: F:Meziantou.Framework.Globbing.GlobDialect.MSBuild
member.summary: Use MSBuild glob pattern syntax: *, ? and **, where both / and \ are path separators and %XX escapes a character. A file name made of *.* matches every file, including the ones without an extension, a leading .. is kept, and a leading separator makes the pattern absolute. Wildcards match a leading dot.

member.name: F:Meziantou.Framework.Globbing.GlobDialect.Posix
member.summary: Use POSIX fnmatch pattern syntax without path-separator awareness, as fnmatch with no flag: the pattern matches a plain string, and *, ? and bracket expressions also match a /. Bracket expressions support ^ as a negation, escapes, character classes such as [[:alpha:]], equivalence classes such as [[=a=]] and collating symbols such as [[.-.]], and a [ that does not open a complete bracket expression is an ordinary character.

member.name: F:Meziantou.Framework.Globbing.GlobDialect.PosixPath
member.summary: Use POSIX fnmatch pattern syntax where ordinary wildcards do not cross path separators, as fnmatch with FNM_PATHNAME: a / is only matched by a / of the pattern, and every / is significant, including a leading one. The syntax is the one of .
